metadata.title: Shape transitions and rare reversals in the elephant random walk
metadata.author: Arjun Pemmasani
metadata.abstract: For every initial bias, the elephant random walk has at most two modal plateaus at finite time and at most two local maxima in its superdiffusive limit. The proof controls first differences and their boundary histories. For a fair first step, a second-difference bound gives a sharper alternative: a unimodal density with two inflection points, or a bimodal density with four. Bimodality holds without computation for memory $a\ge4/5$. A certified computation classifies the fair-start law outside an interval shorter than $3.3\cdot10^{-15}$ around $a=0.6688128600146$; uniqueness of a transition inside remains open. The interval structure of bimodal initial biases also remains open. As $a\to1$, a two-component Landau approximation holds uniformly over the initial bias, in total variation and scaled uniform density distance. It determines the locations and heights of the fair-start peaks. For rare reversals, an explicit total variation approximation by a truncated Luria--Delbr\"uck law gives a Landau local limit theorem with a rate. When $\log N\le x=N\varepsilon\le2\log N$, every mode lies at distance $x\log x+\lambda_{\mathrm L}x+O(\sqrt{x\log x})$ from an end. For even $N$, the origin and each end are equally likely at a unique reversal probability, with $N\varepsilon=2\log N-\log\log N-\log16+o(1)$. At this crossing, every even $N\ge8$ has two symmetric modal intervals and a unique interior minimum, by finite certified computations and analytic bounds.
